version\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent, FilesystemPermission\nfrom deepagents.backends import CompositeBackend, StateBackend, StoreBackend\nfrom langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver\nfrom langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore\n\ncheckpointer = MemorySaver()\nstore = InMemoryStore()\n\nbackend = CompositeBackend(\n    default=StateBackend(),\n    routes={\n        \"/memories/\": StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)),\n    },\n)\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n    tools=[internet_search],\n    system_prompt=(\n        \"You are a research assistant. \"\n        \"Use planning, preserve evidence, and produce source-backed outputs.\"\n    ),\n    backend=backend,\n    store=store,\n    memory=[\"/memories/AGENTS.md\"],\n    permissions=[\n        FilesystemPermission(\n            operations=[\"write\"],\n            paths=[\"/memories/**\"],\n            mode=\"allow\",\n        )\n    ],\n    interrupt_on={\n        \"write_file\": {\"allowed_decisions\": [\"approve\", \"edit\", \"reject\"]},\n        \"edit_file\": {\"allowed_decisions\": [\"approve\", \"edit\", \"reject\"]},\n    },\n    checkpointer=checkpointer,\n    name=\"research-assistant\",\n)\n```\n\nWhy this shape:\n- `StateBackend()` keeps ephemeral scratch and offloaded large tool results thread-scoped.\n- `StoreBackend(...)` gives persistent per-user memory.\n- `interrupt_on` ensures human review for destructive or persistent writes.\n- `checkpointer` is required for interrupt/resume.\n\nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/memory  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n---\n\n## 5) Filesystem backends: what to use and when\n\nDeep Agents exposes a pluggable virtual filesystem. The major built-in backend classes currently documented in the Python reference/docs are:\n\n- `StateBackend`\n- `FilesystemBackend`\n- `StoreBackend`\n- `CompositeBackend`\n- `LocalShellBackend`\n- `ContextHubBackend`\n\nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/\n\n## Recommended default: `StateBackend()`\n\n### Class\n`StateBackend`\n\n### What it does\nStores files in LangGraph agent state for the current thread. Persists across turns in the same thread through checkpoints, but not across threads.  \nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/state/StateBackend\n\n### Best use\nUse it as the **default scratch workspace** for research:\n- query notes\n- intermediate extraction files\n- offloaded tool results\n- temporary summaries\n\n### Why\nResearch agents generate lots of intermediate text; thread-scoped ephemeral storage is exactly the safe default.\n\n---\n\n## `FilesystemBackend(root_dir=..., virtual_mode=True)`\n\n### Class\n`FilesystemBackend`\n\n### Key parameters mentioned in docs\n- `root_dir`\n- `virtual_mode=True`\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### What it does\nReads/writes actual files on disk under a configurable root. With `virtual_mode=True`, paths are sandboxed/normalized under `root_dir`. The docs explicitly warn that `virtual_mode=False` provides no security even if `root_dir` is set.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### Recommendation\nUse only if the assistant must interact with a local project or shared mounted volume. If used:\n- prefer `virtual_mode=True`\n- prefer placing it behind `CompositeBackend`\n- do **not** use it alone for production web APIs\n\n### Important warning\nDeep Agents writes internal artifacts such as:\n- `/large_tool_results/`\n- `/conversation_history/`\n\nIf you use a plain `FilesystemBackend`, those land on disk too. Docs recommend wrapping it in `CompositeBackend` to keep internal artifacts separate.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### Recommended pattern\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents.backends import CompositeBackend, StateBackend, FilesystemBackend\n\nbackend = CompositeBackend(\n    default=StateBackend(),\n    routes={\n        \"/workspace/\": FilesystemBackend(\n            root_dir=\"/path/to/project\",\n            virtual_mode=True,\n        ),\n    },\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n---\n\n## `StoreBackend(namespace=...)`\n\n### Class\n`StoreBackend`\n\n### What it does\nStores files in LangGraph `BaseStore`, enabling durable, cross-thread persistence.  \nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/store/StoreBackend\n\n### Important parameter\n- `namespace=lambda rt: (...)`\n\nThe namespace factory receives a LangGraph `Runtime` and returns `tuple[str, ...]`. The docs strongly recommend explicit namespacing for multi-user deployments.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### Best use\nUse for:\n- durable user memory\n- saved research profiles\n- persistent source inventories\n- team-shared read-only policy content\n\n### Recommended namespace pattern\nFor per-user persistence:\n\n```python\nStoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,))\n```\n\nFor per-assistant shared persistence:\n\n```python\nStoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.assistant_id,))\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### Caution\nThe docs say the legacy default namespace can cause all users of the same assistant to share storage. For multi-user production, set `namespace` explicitly.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n---\n\n## `CompositeBackend(default=..., routes=...)`\n\n### Class\n`CompositeBackend`\n\n### Key parameters\n- `default=...`\n- `routes={...}`\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### What it does\nRoutes file operations to different backends by path prefix.\n\n### Best use\nThis is the **best overall choice** for a research assistant because it separates:\n- ephemeral scratch work\n- durable memory\n- optional local project files\n\n### Recommended layout\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents.backends import CompositeBackend, StateBackend, StoreBackend\n\nbackend = CompositeBackend(\n    default=StateBackend(),\n    routes={\n        \"/memories/\": StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)),\n    },\n)\n```\n\nIf you also need project files:\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents.backends import FilesystemBackend\n\nbackend = CompositeBackend(\n    default=StateBackend(),\n    routes={\n        \"/workspace/\": FilesystemBackend(root_dir=\"/srv/research-workspace\", virtual_mode=True),\n        \"/memories/\": StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)),\n    },\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n---\n\n## `LocalShellBackend(root_dir=..., env=...)`\n\n### Class\n`LocalShellBackend`\n\n### Key parameters from docs\n- `root_dir`\n- `virtual_mode`\n- `env`\n- supports `timeout` and `max_output_bytes`\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### What it does\nAdds unrestricted host shell execution via the `execute` tool.\n\n### Recommendation\nDo **not** use this in production for a research assistant exposed to end users. The docs explicitly warn it is only suitable for controlled development environments.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n---\n\n## `ContextHubBackend(\"repo\")`\n\n### Class\n`ContextHubBackend`\n\n### What it does\nStores filesystem contents durably in a LangSmith Context Hub repo.  \nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/context_hub/ContextHubBackend\n\n### Best use\nUse this if your team is already centered on LangSmith Context Hub and wants versioned shared context, instructions, or skills without provisioning a separate store.\n\n---\n\n## Backend recommendation summary\n\nFor this project:\n\n### Preferred\n**`CompositeBackend(default=StateBackend(), routes={\"/memories/\": StoreBackend(...)})`**\n\n### Optional\nAdd `\"/workspace/\" -> FilesystemBackend(..., virtual_mode=True)` only if real project file access is required.\n\n### Avoid\n`LocalShellBackend` in production.\n\n---\n\n## 6) How to define subagents\n\nDeep Agents supports synchronous subagents via the `task` tool, with two primary formats:\n\n1. **Dictionary-based `SubAgent` spec**\n2. **`CompiledSubAgent`** wrapping a pre-built LangGraph/LangChain runnable\n\nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \n- https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/middleware/subagents/SubAgent  \n- https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/middleware/subagents/CompiledSubAgent\n\n## Default behavior: `general-purpose` subagent\n\nDeep Agents automatically inserts a synchronous **`general-purpose`** subagent unless you provide one with that name yourself.  \nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \n- https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph\n\nThis default is useful, but for a production research assistant you should define explicit specialized subagents rather than relying only on the generic one.\n\n---\n\n## Dictionary-based `SubAgent`\n\n### Supported fields documented\n- `name: str`\n- `description: str`\n- `system_prompt: str`\n- `tools: list[Callable]` (optional)\n- `model: str | BaseChatModel` (optional)\n- `middleware: list[Middleware]` (optional)\n- `interrupt_on: dict[str, bool | InterruptOnConfig]` (optional)\n- `skills: list[str]` (optional)\n- `response_format` (optional)\n- `permissions: list[FilesystemPermission]` (optional)\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n### Recommended subagent layout for research\nUse at least three subagents:\n\n1. **source-finder**\n   - searches broadly\n   - collects candidate sources\n2. **evidence-extractor**\n   - reads source material\n   - extracts claims, numbers, quotes, dates\n3. **report-writer**\n   - synthesizes evidence into final structured report\n\n### Example\n\n```python\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field\n\nclass ResearchFindings(BaseModel):\n    summary: str = Field(description=\"Summary of findings\")\n    confidence: float = Field(description=\"Confidence from 0 to 1\")\n    sources: list[str] = Field(description=\"Source URLs\")\n\nsource_finder = {\n    \"name\": \"source-finder\",\n    \"description\": \"Finds and prioritizes relevant sources for a research topic.\",\n    \"system_prompt\": (\n        \"Search broadly, prioritize authoritative sources, \"\n        \"and return a concise list of relevant URLs with rationale.\"\n    ),\n    \"tools\": [internet_search],\n    \"model\": \"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n}\n\nevidence_extractor = {\n    \"name\": \"evidence-extractor\",\n    \"description\": \"Extracts evidence and claims from source material.\",\n    \"system_prompt\": (\n        \"Read sources carefully, extract factual claims, \"\n        \"capture dates, figures, and direct citations.\"\n    ),\n    \"tools\": [internet_search],\n    \"response_format\": ResearchFindings,\n}\n\nreport_writer = {\n    \"name\": \"report-writer\",\n    \"description\": \"Synthesizes evidence into a final answer with citations.\",\n    \"system_prompt\": (\n        \"Write a clear research report. Distinguish facts from inference. \"\n        \"Cite all claims with source URLs.\"\n    ),\n}\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```python\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n    tools=[internet_search],\n    subagents=[source_finder, evidence_extractor, report_writer],\n)\n```\n\nGrounding for field names and structured output support:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n---\n\n## `CompiledSubAgent`\n\nUse `CompiledSubAgent` when you already have a custom LangChain agent or LangGraph workflow.\n\n### Required fields\n- `name`\n- `description`\n- `runnable`\n\nThe runnable must be a compiled graph and its state schema must include a `\"messages\"` key.  \nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \n- https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/middleware/subagents/CompiledSubAgent\n\n### Example\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent, CompiledSubAgent\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\n\ncustom_graph = create_agent(\n    model=your_model,\n    tools=specialized_tools,\n    prompt=\"You are a specialized agent for evidence extraction.\",\n)\n\ncustom_subagent = CompiledSubAgent(\n    name=\"evidence-extractor\",\n    description=\"Specialized agent for extracting evidence from research material\",\n    runnable=custom_graph,\n)\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n    tools=[internet_search],\n    subagents=[custom_subagent],\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n### Engineering recommendation\nStart with dictionary subagents. Move to `CompiledSubAgent` only if:\n- you need a custom graph\n- you need nontrivial internal control flow\n- you already own a reusable LangChain/LangGraph agent\n\n---\n\n## Controlling the default `general-purpose` subagent\n\nIf you want no generic delegation, disable it through a harness profile using:\n\n- `GeneralPurposeSubagentProfile(enabled=False)`\n\nThe docs say this is the supported way to remove the built-in `task` path when no synchronous subagents remain.  \nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \n- https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/profiles/harness/harness_profiles/GeneralPurposeSubagentProfile\n\n---\n\n## 7) Human-in-the-loop support\n\nDeep Agents supports human approval using LangGraph interrupts.\n\n## Main configuration surface: `interrupt_on`\n\nPass `interrupt_on` to `create_deep_agent(...)` as:\n\n```python\ninterrupt_on={\n    \"tool_name\": True | False | {\"allowed_decisions\": [...]}\n}\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### Supported decision types\nThe docs list:\n- `approve`\n- `edit`\n- `reject`\n- `respond`\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### Simple example\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\nfrom langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver\n\ncheckpointer = MemorySaver()\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n    tools=[internet_search],\n    interrupt_on={\n        \"write_file\": True,\n        \"edit_file\": {\"allowed_decisions\": [\"approve\", \"edit\", \"reject\"]},\n    },\n    checkpointer=checkpointer,\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## Critical requirement: checkpointer\n\nThe docs are explicit: **a checkpointer is required for human-in-the-loop**.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## Resume flow\n\nWhen interrupted, invoke with a stable `thread_id`, inspect `result.interrupts`, then resume with:\n\n```python\nfrom langgraph.types import Command\n\nagent.invoke(\n    Command(resume={\"decisions\": decisions}),\n    config=config,\n    version=\"v2\",\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## Conditional interrupts\n\nPython supports a `when` predicate in `InterruptOnConfig` so only certain tool calls pause.\n\nExample from docs pattern:\n\n```python\ndef writes_outside_workspace(request: ToolCallRequest) -> bool:\n    path = request.tool_call[\"args\"].get(\"file_path\", \"\")\n    return not path.startswith(\"/workspace/\")\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## Filesystem permission interrupts\n\nIn addition to `interrupt_on`, filesystem permission rules can use:\n\n```python\nFilesystemPermission(\n    operations=[\"write\"],\n    paths=[\"/secrets/**\"],\n    mode=\"interrupt\",\n)\n```\n\nThis requires `deepagents>=0.6.8`.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### Recommendation for this project\nEnable human review for:\n- `write_file`\n- `edit_file`\n- any email/outbound notification tool\n- any persistent memory write path\n- any export/publish tool\n\nDo not require approval for:\n- `read_file`\n- `ls`\n- `glob`\n- `grep`\n- search tools\n\n---\n\n## 8) Recommended architecture for this specific research assistant\n\n## Main agent responsibilities\nThe top-level agent should:\n- interpret the user request\n- create/maintain a todo plan using built-in planning behavior\n- delegate expensive or context-heavy tasks to subagents\n- maintain artifacts in filesystem\n- synthesize a final report\n\n## Suggested tooling\nAt minimum:\n- `internet_search(...)`\n- optional `fetch_url(...)` / page retrieval tool\n- optional document parsing tools\n- optional citation normalization tool\n\nThe exact tool set is application-specific, but Deep Agents is designed for custom tools and MCP tools passed via `tools=`.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/customization\n\n## Suggested backend design\n\n```python\nCompositeBackend(\n    default=StateBackend(),\n    routes={\n        \"/memories/\": StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)),\n        # optionally:\n        # \"/workspace/\": FilesystemBackend(root_dir=\"/srv/workspace\", virtual_mode=True),\n    },\n)\n```\n\nRationale:\n- default scratch remains ephemeral\n- memory persists per user\n- project workspace can be added later if needed\n\nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/memory\n\n## Suggested subagents\n- `source-finder`\n- `fact-checker`\n- `evidence-extractor`\n- `report-writer`\n\nFor structured coordination, give `fact-checker` or `evidence-extractor` a `response_format` schema.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n## Suggested guardrails\n- `interrupt_on` for persistent writes and publication actions\n- `permissions` to deny writes to protected paths\n- read-only policies stored separately from writable memory\n- explicit store namespacing per user or per assistant+user\n\nSources:  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/memory\n\n---\n\n## 9) Concrete implementation sketch\n\n```python\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent, \nSources: PyPI project page https://pypi.org/project/deepagents ; LangChain overview https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview ; Python reference reference and docs  \nhttps://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent  \nhttps://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview\n\n### Minimal example from the docs pattern\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\n\ndef get_weather(city: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Get weather for a given city.\"\"\"\n    return f\"It's always sunny in {city}!\"\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n    tools=[get_weather],\n    system_prompt=\"You are a helpful assistant\",\n)\n\nresult = agent.invoke({\n    \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"What's the weather in SF?\"}]\n})\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview\n\n### Key parameters you should design around\n\nThe official reference and docs confirm these parameter names:\n\n- **`model`** \u2014 model identifier or model object  \n- **`tools`** \u2014 list of tools exposed to the agent\n- **`system_prompt`** \u2014 custom instructions\n- **`backend`** \u2014 filesystem backend\n- **`subagents`** \u2014 delegated agents exposed through the built-in `task` tool\n- **`interrupt_on`** \u2014 human approval configuration by tool name\n- **`checkpointer`** \u2014 required for human-in-the-loop / interrupt flows\n\nSources:  \nhttps://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent  \nhttps://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \nhttps://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \nhttps://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### What `create_deep_agent` gives you by default\n\nDeep Agents includes built-in capabilities beyond plain tool-calling:\n\n- planning / todo management,\n- filesystem tools (`ls`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `glob`, `grep`),\n- subagent delegation via a built-in **`task`** tool,\n- LangGraph-based execution and streaming.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview\n\n### Recommended top-level constructor for your use case\n\nFor a research assistant, the main agent should be the coordinator, not the heavy retriever. Use it to plan, delegate, and synthesize.\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n    tools=[web_search_tool, fetch_url_tool, citation_resolver_tool],\n    system_prompt=(\n        \"You are a research assistant. \"\n        \"Ground every claim in cited sources, prefer authoritative sources, \"\n        \"use subagents for deep retrieval, and save intermediate artifacts to files.\"\n    ),\n    backend=...,          # choose persistent backend\n    subagents=[...],      # define specialized workers\n    interrupt_on={...},   # guard write/publish actions\n    checkpointer=...,     # required if interrupt_on is used\n)\n```\n\nThis pattern is directly aligned with the product\u2019s intended use: planning, file-backed context management, and subagent delegation.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview\n\n---\n\n## 3) Filesystem backends\n\nDeep Agents exposes a filesystem surface to the model and lets you swap the storage backend. The official backends page lists these options.\n\n### Official backend options\n\n#### A. Default thread-scoped backend\nIf you do not pass `backend=...`, the default filesystem is stored in LangGraph state and is thread-scoped.\n\n```python\nagent = create_deep_agent(model=\"google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash\")\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n**Use when:** quick experiments only.  \n**Do not use for:** production research workflows where notes/artifacts must persist across runs.\n\n---\n\n#### B. `FilesystemBackend`\nGives the agent access to the local machine filesystem under a root directory.\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents.backends import FilesystemBackend\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash\",\n    backend=FilesystemBackend(root_dir=\"/Users/nh/Desktop/\")\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n**Exact class / parameter names confirmed:**\n- class: **`FilesystemBackend`**\n- constructor kwarg: **`root_dir`**\n\n**Use when:** you want local persistent artifacts such as:\n- downloaded source excerpts,\n- extracted notes,\n- citation ledgers,\n- draft reports.\n\n**Engineering note:** scope `root_dir` to a dedicated workspace, not a general home directory.\n\n---\n\n#### C. `StoreBackend`\nPersists files in a LangGraph store across threads.\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash\",\n    backend=StoreBackend()\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n**Use when:** you need durable, multi-thread memory without coupling to a local disk path.\n\n---\n\n#### D. `ContextHubBackend`\nStores files durably in a LangSmith Hub repo.\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents.backends import ContextHubBackend\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash\",\n    backend=ContextHubBackend(\"my-agent\")\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n**Use when:** you want durable shared context without provisioning a separate store.\n\n---\n\n#### E. `LocalShellBackend`\nCombines host filesystem access and shell execution.\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents.backends import LocalShellBackend\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash\",\n    backend=LocalShellBackend(\n        root_dir=\".\",\n        env={\"PATH\": \"/usr/bin:/bin\"}\n    )\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n**Use when:** you need code execution or command-line tooling as part of research.  \n**Risk:** highest local security exposure.\n\n---\n\n### Filesystem recommendation for your research assistant\n\nFor production, prefer one of these two patterns:\n\n#### Recommended default\n- **`StoreBackend()`** if you want durable artifacts across threads and environments.\n\n#### Recommended for local/internal deployments\n- **`FilesystemBackend(root_dir=...)`** if the team wants direct file inspection and external tooling integration.\n\n### Filesystem permissions\n\nThe docs also support **`FilesystemPermission`** rules via the `permissions=` parameter to `create_deep_agent(...)`.\n\nExample from the docs:\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import FilesystemPermission, create_deep_agent\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=model,\n    backend=backend,\n    permissions=[\n        FilesystemPermission(\n            operations=[\"write\"],\n            paths=[\"/**\"],\n            mode=\"deny\",\n        ),\n    ],\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/permissions\n\nFor your assistant, use permissions to:\n- deny writes outside the workspace,\n- deny reads of secrets or config folders,\n- optionally make evidence repositories read-only.\n\n---\n\n## 4) How to define subagents\n\nSubagents are central to a research assistant because they isolate bulky retrieval work from the coordinator context. The official docs say subagents are configured through the **`subagents`** parameter and invoked by the built-in **`task()`** tool.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n### Why use subagents here\n\nThe docs explicitly describe the benefit: when tools return large outputs, subagents keep the main context clean because the main agent receives only the final result rather than all intermediate calls.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n### Declarative subagent spec\n\nThe reference page for **`SubAgent`** confirms these fields:\n\n- **`name`**\n- **`description`**\n- **`prompt`**\n- **`tools`**\n- **`model`**\n- **`middleware`**\n- **`interrupt_on`**\n- **`skills`**\n- **`permissions`**\n- **`response_format`**\n\nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/middleware/subagents/SubAgent\n\nA practical definition looks like:\n\n```python\nresearch_subagent = {\n    \"name\": \"source-researcher\",\n    \"description\": \"Finds authoritative sources and returns concise evidence summaries.\",\n    \"prompt\": (\n        \"You are a specialist research subagent. \"\n        \"Search broadly, prefer primary sources, and return cited findings only.\"\n    ),\n    \"tools\": [web_search_tool, fetch_url_tool],\n    \"model\": \"anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001\",\n}\n```\n\nThe docs confirm that if **`tools`** is not specified, the subagent can inherit from the main agent.  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/middleware/subagents/SubAgent\n\n### `CompiledSubAgent`\n\nThe reference also distinguishes **`CompiledSubAgent`** entries, which expose a pre-built runnable through the `task` tool instead of a declarative prompt/tools config.  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\nUse `CompiledSubAgent` when you already have a custom LangGraph workflow and want to attach it as a worker.\n\n---\n\n## 5) Recommended subagent layout for a research assistant\n\nUse at least three subagents:\n\n### 1. `source-researcher`\n**Purpose:** find candidate sources and rank them by authority.\n\nSuggested config:\n- tools: web search, URL fetch\n- model: cheaper/faster model acceptable\n- output: structured list of sources and rationale\n\n### 2. `evidence-extractor`\n**Purpose:** read long pages/documents and extract precise claims with citations.\n\nSuggested config:\n- tools: fetch/read tools\n- permissions: read-only\n- output: structured evidence objects\n\n### 3. `report-synthesizer`\n**Purpose:** combine evidence into a polished answer or report section.\n\nSuggested config:\n- minimal tools\n- stronger model\n- optional `response_format` for schema-controlled output\n\nThis matches the documented rationale for subagents: context quarantine and specialization.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n---\n\n## 6) Human-in-the-loop support\n\nDeep Agents supports human approval for tool execution. The official Python human-in-the-loop docs show:\n\n- **`interrupt_on`** passed to `create_deep_agent(...)`\n- a **checkpointer is required**\n- tool-level config can be boolean or a config object with **`allowed_decisions`**\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### Official pattern\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\nfrom langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver\n\ncheckpointer = MemorySaver()\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash\",\n    tools=[remove_file, fetch_file, notify_email],\n    interrupt_on={\n        \"remove_file\": True,   # default decisions: approve, edit, reject, respond\n        \"fetch_file\": False,   # no interrupt\n        \"notify_email\": {\n            \"allowed_decisions\": [\"approve\", \"reject\"]\n        },\n    },\n    checkpointer=checkpointer,  # required\n)\n```\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### Exact names confirmed\n- **`interrupt_on`**\n- **`checkpointer`**\n- **`allowed_decisions`**\n- default decisions include: **`approve`**, **`edit`**, **`reject`**, **`respond`**\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### Recommended HITL policy for your assistant\n\nRequire approval for:\n- `write_file`\n- `edit_file`\n- destructive tools like `remove_file`\n- any outbound action: email, Slack, CMS publish, PR creation\n- any billing-sensitive or privileged API tool\n\nSuggested config:\n\n```python\ninterrupt_on = {\n    \"write_file\": True,\n    \"edit_file\": True,\n    \"remove_file\": {\"allowed_decisions\": [\"approve\", \"reject\"]},\n    \"publish_report\": {\"allowed_decisions\": [\"approve\", \"edit\", \"reject\"]},\n}\n```\n\n### Why this matters for research\nA research assistant will often produce artifacts that humans need to inspect:\n- source memos,\n- draft reports,\n- citation tables,\n- final deliverables.\n\nHITL is the cleanest way to keep the agent autonomous in retrieval while retaining editorial control over outputs.\n\n---\n\n## 7) Proposed implementation blueprint\n\n### Main agent responsibilities\nThe top-level agent should:\n- interpret the user task,\n- make/track a plan,\n- delegate retrieval to subagents,\n- manage files,\n- synthesize final outputs.\n\n### Suggested code skeleton\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\nfrom deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\nfrom langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver\n\ncheckpointer = MemorySaver()\n\nsource_researcher = {\n    \"name\": \"source-researcher\",\n    \"description\": \"Finds authoritative sources for a research query.\",\n    \"prompt\": (\n        \"Search for authoritative sources. Prefer primary and official sources. \"\n        \"Return concise findings with URLs.\"\n    ),\n    \"tools\": [web_search_tool, fetch_url_tool],\n    \"model\": \"anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001\",\n}\n\nevidence_extractor = {\n    \"name\": \"evidence-extractor\",\n    \"description\": \"Reads source material and extracts precise claims with citations.\",\n    \"prompt\": (\n        \"Extract only supported claims. Quote or summarize faithfully and include source URLs.\"\n    ),\n    \"tools\": [fetch_url_tool],\n}\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n    tools=[web_search_tool, fetch_url_tool, citation_resolver_tool],\n    system_prompt=(\n        \"You are a research assistant. Every substantive claim must be grounded in sources. \"\n        \"Use subagents for retrieval and extraction. Save working notes and drafts to files.\"\n    ),\n    backend=StoreBackend(),\n    subagents=[source_researcher, evidence_extractor],\n    interrupt_on={\n        \"write_file\": True,\n        \"edit_file\": True,\n    },\n    checkpointer=checkpointer,\n)\n```\n\nThis is the closest production-oriented shape to what the official docs support today.  \nSources:  \nhttps://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent  \nhttps://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \nhttps://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \nhttps://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n---\n\n## 8) Engineering decisions and tradeoffs\n\n### Model strategy\nUse a stronger model for the coordinator and synthesis layer, and cheaper models for retrieval-oriented subagents. The `SubAgent` reference confirms per-subagent **`model`** overrides.  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/middleware/subagents/SubAgent\n\n### Storage strategy\n- **Best default:** `StoreBackend()` for persistence across threads.\n- **Best local/dev option:** `FilesystemBackend(root_dir=...)`.\n- **Avoid default thread-scoped state** for serious research workflows.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### Safety strategy\nUse both:\n- **filesystem permissions** for path-level enforcement,\n- **interrupt_on** for action approval.  \nSources:  \nhttps://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/permissions  \nhttps://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### Observability\nThe docs recommend LangSmith tracing to inspect planning steps, tool calls, and subagent delegation.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/quickstart\n\n---\n\n## 9) Risks to account for\n\n1. **Rapid API evolution**  \n   Pin `deepagents==0.6.12` and test against that exact version.  \n   Source: https://pypi.org/project/deepagents\n\n2. **Host filesystem exposure**  \n   `FilesystemBackend` and especially `LocalShellBackend` can expose real resources; constrain scope tightly.  \n   Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n3. **Unreviewed artifact generation**  \n   Without `interrupt_on`, the agent may write or modify files automatically.  \n   Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n4. **Context overload without subagents**  \n   The subagents docs explicitly call out context contamination from large tool outputs.  \n   Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n---\n\n## 10) Example usage is via:\n\n```python\nreasoning={\"effort\": \"low\"}\n```\n\nSource: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning\n\nOpenAI\u2019s model catalog and model pages show reasoning-effort controls for GPT-5 family models:\n\n### GPT-5 family reasoning-effort support\n\n| Model | Supported `reasoning.effort` values |\n|---|---|\n| `gpt-5.5` | `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` |\n| `gpt-5.4` | `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` |\n| `gpt-5.4-mini` | `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` |\n| `gpt-5.4-nano` | `none` (default), `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` |\n| `gpt-5.5-pro` | `medium`, `high` (default), `xhigh` |\n| `gpt-5.4-pro` | `medium` (default), `high`, `xhigh` |\n\nSources:  \n- `gpt-5.5` / `gpt-5.4` / `gpt-5.4-mini` overview: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models  \n- `gpt-5.4-nano`: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-nano  \n- `gpt-5.5-pro`: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.5-pro  \n- `gpt-5.4-pro`: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-pro\n\n**Important cost implication:** OpenAI\u2019s reasoning docs state these models use internal reasoning tokens. replacement is:\n\n- `geolocation(request)` from `@vercel/functions`\n- `ipAddress(request)` from `@vercel/functions`\n\n- Source: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15\n\nThis is Refresh\n- different compatibility surface than webpack\n- custom webpack logic may block adoption\n\n### Opt-out\nUse:\n```bash\nnext build --webpack\nnext dev --webpack\n```\n\n- Source: same project\n\n- Source: https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#behavior-changes\n\n### Why you care\nThis can affect:\n- local dev scripts\n- monorepo task runners\n- custom build orchestration\n- CI jobs sharing workspaces\n\n---\n\n## 5.4 Babel behavior under Turbopack changed\nNext.js 16 says Turbopack now **automatically enables Babel if a Babel config is found**; previously it errored hard.\n\n- builds may behave differently or become slower\n- this matters especially if you plan to enable `reactCompiler`\n\nAudit for:\n- `.babelrc`\n- `babel.config.js`\n- package-level Babel configs in monorepos\n\n---\n\n## 5.5 React Compiler support is stable, but not on by default\n`reactCompiler` became a stable config in Next.js 16, promoted from `experimental`, but it is **not enabled by https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16\n\n### Team guidance\nAudit `next.config.js|mjs|ts` for:\n- `webpack(config, context) { ... }`\n- old `experimental.turbo`\n- bundler-specific The upgrade guide explicitly calls out alignment with Async Request APIs and notes that affected surfaces now receive request values such as `params` and `id` as promises in some APIs.  \nSource: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16\n\n### Common impact areas\n- `page.js`\n- `layout.js`\n- `generateMetadata`\n- `searchParams`\n- route-adjacent generation APIs\n- image generation functions\n\n### Example pattern from official docs\nIn affected App Router code, `params` may become:\n\n```ts\ntype Params = Promise<{ slug: string }>\n```\n\nand then be used as:\n\n```ts\nconst { slug } = await params\n```\n\nSource: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15\n\n### Team guidance\nSearch for synchronous access patterns like:\n- `params.slug`\n- `searchParams.foo`\n- metadata functions that destructure sync params\n\nRefactor them to the promise-based shape where required by the v16 docs.\n\n---\n\n## D. \nSource: https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16-1\n\nThis matters for developer experience and can change local cold-start characteristics.\n\n## Build debugging improvements\nNext.js 16.2 added `--inspect` 16 promotes **`cacheComponents`** as the top-level model replacing older experimental knobs like `dynamicIO`.  \nSources: https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16 , backend** that separates project workspace from internal agent artifacts\n- **human-in-the-loop** for write/edit/send/publish actions\n\nA strong default is:\n- main agent: planning + orchestration + final synthesis\n- `researcher` subagent: web research and evidence collection\n- optional `fact-checker` subagent: source validation / contradiction checks\n- optional `report-writer` subagent: convert findings into final structured prose\n\nThis follows the official guidance that subagents are best for context isolation and multi-step subtasks, especially when tools return large outputs.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n---\n\n## 3) Current package version and installation guidance\n\n### Current version\n- **`deepagents==0.6.12`** on PyPI, released **2026-06-25**  \nSource: https://pypi.org/project/deepagents/\n\n### Core install\nAt minimum:\n```bash\npip install -U deepagents\n```\nSource: https://pypi.org/project/deepagents/\n\n### Add a model provider package\nDeep Agents docs show pairing `deepagents` with a LangChain provider package, for example:\n- `langchain-google-genai`\n- `langchain-openai`\n- `langchain-anthropic`  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview\n\nExample:\n```bash\npip install -U deepagents langchain-openai\n```\n\n### Recommendation\nPin the package versions in your application environment for reproducibility. The docs are current, but the profiles API is explicitly marked beta in the reference, so avoid floating major behavior in production without a lockfile.  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/profiles/harness/harness_profiles\n\n---\n\n## 4) Core API: creating an agent\n\n## Main constructor\nThe main API is:\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\n```\n\nThe official reference describes `create_deep_agent` as the main entry point for creating deep agents.  \nSources:  \n- Agent overview in reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/agent  \n- Function reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\n## Current function signature\nThe docs/reference show this parameter surface for `create_deep_agent`:\n\n- `model`\n- `tools`\n- `system_prompt`\n- `middleware`\n- `subagents`\n- `skills`\n- `memory`\n- `permissions`\n- `backend`\n- `interrupt_on`\n- `response_format`\n- `state_schema`\n- `context_schema`\n- `checkpointer`\n- `store`\n- `debug`\n- `name`\n- `cache`\n\nSpecifically, the reference lists:\n\n```python\ncreate_deep_agent(\n    model: str | BaseChatModel | None = None,\n    tools: Sequence[BaseTool | Callable | dict[str, Any]] | None = None,\n    *,\n    system_prompt: str | SystemMessage | None = None,\n    middleware: Sequence[AgentMiddleware] = (),\n    subagents: Sequence[SubAgent | CompiledSubAgent | AsyncSubAgent] | None = None,\n    skills: list[str] | None = None,\n    memory: list[str] | None = None,\n    permissions: list[FilesystemPermission] | None = None,\n    backend: BackendProtocol | BackendFactory | None = None,\n    interrupt_on: dict[str, bool | InterruptOnConfig] | None = None,\n    response_format: ResponseFormat[...] | type[...] | dict[str, Any] | None = None,\n    state_schema: type[DeepAgentState] | None = None,\n    context_schema: type[ContextT] | None = None,\n    checkpointer: Checkpointer | None = None,\n    store: BaseStore | None = None,\n    debug: bool = False,\n    name: str | None = None,\n    cache: BaseCache | None = None,\n) -> CompiledStateGraph[...]\n```\n\nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\n## Important API notes\n### `model`\nThe docs recommend passing a `provider:model` string such as:\n- `\"openai:gpt-5.5\"`\n- `\"google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash\"`\n- `\"anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6\"`  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview\n\nThe reference also states:\n- `model=None` is deprecated since `0.5.3`\n- relying on the default model will be removed in `deepagents==1.0.0`  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\n### `tools`\n`tools=` is additive. It does **not** remove built-in tools. To remove built-ins, the reference says to use a `HarnessProfile` with `excluded_tools`.  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\n### Built-in tools\nBy default, the agent has:\n- `write_todos`\n- `ls`\n- `read_file`\n- `write_file`\n- `edit_file`\n- `glob`\n- `grep`\n- `execute`\n- `task`\n\n`execute` only works if the backend supports sandbox execution; otherwise it returns an error.  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\n---\n\n## 5) Minimal implementation pattern\n\nA minimal research assistant should be built like this:\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\n\ndef internet_search(query: str, max_results: int = 5, topic: str = \"general\", include_raw_content: bool = False):\n    \"\"\"Run a web search.\"\"\"\n    ...\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n    tools=[internet_search],\n    system_prompt=(\n        \"You are a research assistant. \"\n        \"Break complex requests into tasks, gather evidence, keep notes in files, \"\n        \"and return cited findings.\"\n    ),\n    name=\"research-assistant\",\n)\n```\n\nThis aligns with the docs\u2019 standard initialization pattern and keeps the search capability as an explicit custom tool.  \nSources:  \n- Overview quickstart: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview  \n- Customization: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/customization\n\n### Invocation pattern\nDocs show invocation in the form:\n```python\nagent.invoke({\n    \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Research topic X\"}]\n})\n```\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview\n\nFor production or any stateful workflow, carry a `thread_id` in:\n```python\nconfig={\"configurable\": {\"thread_id\": \"...\"}}\n```\nThis matters for persistence, subagent continuity, and especially human-in-the-loop resume flows.  \nSources:  \n- Human-in-the-loop: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop  \n- Going to production: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/going-to-production\n\n---\n\n## 6) Filesystem backends: what to use and why\n\nDeep Agents exposes a pluggable filesystem layer behind the built-in file tools. The official backends docs recommend choosing a backend based on durability and execution needs.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n## Available built-in backends\n\n### 6.1 `StateBackend`\n- Default backend when `backend=` is omitted\n- Thread-scoped\n- Files persist across turns in the same thread through checkpointing\n- Files are **not** shared across threads  \nSources:  \n- Backends guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- Reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/state/StateBackend\n\nUse when:\n- research notes are ephemeral per conversation\n- you want a scratchpad and automatic offloading of large tool outputs\n\n### 6.2 `FilesystemBackend`\n- Reads/writes real files under a `root_dir`\n- Supports `virtual_mode=True`\n- Docs strongly recommend `virtual_mode=True` for path restriction\n- `root_dir` must be absolute in the documented local-disk example text  \nSources:  \n- Backends guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- Reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/filesystem/FilesystemBackend\n\nUse when:\n- you want research outputs on local disk\n- your engineering team needs generated files in a project folder\n\nCaution:\nThe docs explicitly warn that using `FilesystemBackend` alone causes internal files like `/large_tool_results/` and `/conversation_history/` to be written to real disk under `root_dir`.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### 6.3 `StoreBackend`\n- Persists files across threads using LangGraph `BaseStore`\n- Intended for durable storage\n- Requires a `store=` at agent creation unless platform-provisioned  \nSources:  \n- Backends guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- Reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/store/StoreBackend\n\nUse when:\n- you want long-lived research memory\n- users should reuse prior findings or cached evidence across sessions\n\n### 6.4 `ContextHubBackend`\n- Persists files in a LangSmith Context Hub repo\n- Useful for LangSmith-native durable storage and commit history  \nSources:  \n- Backends guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- Reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/context_hub/ContextHubBackend\n\n### 6.5 `CompositeBackend`\n- Routes different path prefixes to different backends\n- Longer prefixes win\n- Recommended by docs for separating workspace files from internal artifacts  \nSources:  \n- Backends guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- Reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/composite/CompositeBackend\n\n### 6.6 `LocalShellBackend`\n- Extends filesystem access with unrestricted local shell execution\n- Docs warn this is for controlled development only\n- Shell commands run directly on the host  \nSources:  \n- Backends guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- Reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/local_shell/LocalShellBackend\n\n---\n\n## 7) Recommended backend choice for this research assistant\n\nFor a research assistant, the best default design is:\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents.backends import CompositeBackend, StateBackend, FilesystemBackend\n\nbackend = CompositeBackend(\n    default=StateBackend(),\n    routes={\n        \"/workspace/\": FilesystemBackend(\n            root_dir=\"/absolute/path/to/project\",\n            virtual_mode=True,\n        ),\n    },\n)\n```\n\nWhy:\n- `/workspace/` maps to real project files\n- internal artifacts remain in `StateBackend`\n- agent-generated drafts and notes are visible to engineers\n- offloaded large results and conversation history stay out of the project tree\n\nThis is directly aligned with the official docs\u2019 recommendation to wrap `FilesystemBackend` in `CompositeBackend`.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\nIf cross-thread memory is important, add a durable route such as:\n```python\nfrom deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\n\nbackend = CompositeBackend(\n    default=StateBackend(),\n    routes={\n        \"/workspace/\": FilesystemBackend(root_dir=\"/absolute/path/to/project\", virtual_mode=True),\n        \"/memories/\": StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)),\n    },\n)\n```\n\nThat pattern is also documented.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n---\n\n## 8) Defining subagents\n\nDeep Agents supports three subagent forms through `subagents=`:\n1. `SubAgent` (declarative synchronous spec)\n2. `CompiledSubAgent` (pre-compiled runnable/graph)\n3. `AsyncSubAgent` (remote/background Agent Protocol subagent)\n\nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\nFor this project, focus on **declarative synchronous subagents** first.\n\n## 8.1 Declarative subagents: field names\nThe docs list these dictionary fields for a `SubAgent` spec:\n\n- `name` \u2014 required\n- `description` \u2014 required\n- `system_prompt` \u2014 required\n- `tools` \u2014 optional\n- `model` \u2014 optional\n- `middleware` \u2014 optional\n- `interrupt_on` \u2014 optional\n- `skills` \u2014 optional\n- `response_format` \u2014 optional\n- `permissions` \u2014 optional\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\nImportant inheritance rules from the docs:\n- `tools`: inherits from main agent by default; specifying overrides inherited tools\n- `model`: inherits from main agent by default\n- `middleware`: does not inherit from main agent\n- `interrupt_on`: inherits from main agent by default; subagent value overrides\n- `skills`: custom subagents do **not** inherit main-agent skills by default\n- `permissions`: when set, **replaces** the parent agent\u2019s permissions  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n## 8.2 Example subagent spec for research\n```python\nresearch_subagent = {\n    \"name\": \"researcher\",\n    \"description\": \"Conducts in-depth web research and returns concise cited findings.\",\n    \"system_prompt\": (\n        \"You are a thorough researcher. \"\n        \"Break the question into search queries, collect evidence, synthesize findings, \"\n        \"and return a concise answer with source URLs.\"\n    ),\n    \"tools\": [internet_search],\n    \"model\": \"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n}\n```\n\nThis mirrors the documented pattern for dictionary-based subagents.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n## 8.3 `CompiledSubAgent`\nIf your team later wants a custom LangGraph or `create_agent(...)`-based specialist, use `CompiledSubAgent` with:\n- `name`\n- `description`\n- `runnable`\n\nThe docs note the runnable must have a state schema with a `\"messages\"` key.  \nSources:  \n- Subagents docs: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \n- Reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/middleware/subagents/CompiledSubAgent\n\n## 8.4 Default `general-purpose` subagent\nDeep Agents automatically adds a synchronous `general-purpose` subagent unless:\n- you provide your own subagent named `\"general-purpose\"`, or\n- the active harness profile disables it\n\nThis default subagent has filesystem tools by default.  \nSources:  \n- Subagents docs: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \n- Reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\n### Recommendation\nKeep the default `general-purpose` subagent for initial versions, but add an explicit `researcher` subagent so the main agent has a clearly described specialist. The docs emphasize that clear `description` text improves routing decisions.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n---\n\n## 9) Human-in-the-loop support\n\nDeep Agents supports HITL through LangGraph interrupts using the `interrupt_on` parameter in `create_deep_agent`.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## 9.1 Core configuration\n`interrupt_on` is a mapping from tool name to:\n- `True`\n- `False`\n- a custom `InterruptOnConfig`\n\nThe docs define:\n- `True`: enable interrupts with default behavior\n- `False`: disable interrupts\n- `InterruptOnConfig`: custom config, including `allowed_decisions`\n- Python also supports optional `when` predicate for conditional interrupts  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## 9.2 Allowed decisions\nThe docs list these decision types:\n- `approve`\n- `edit`\n- `reject`\n- `respond`\n\nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## 9.3 Checkpointer requirement\nThe docs explicitly state that a **checkpointer is required** for human-in-the-loop pause/resume flows.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\nExample:\n```python\nfrom langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\n\ncheckpointer = MemorySaver()\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n    tools=[internet_search],\n    interrupt_on={\n        \"write_file\": True,\n        \"edit_file\": {\"allowed_decisions\": [\"approve\", \"edit\", \"reject\"]},\n    },\n    checkpointer=checkpointer,\n)\n```\n\nThis is consistent with the docs\u2019 examples.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## 9.4 Resume flow\nThe docs show resuming with:\n```python\nfrom langgraph.types import Command\n\nresult = agent.invoke(\n    Command(resume={\"decisions\": decisions}),\n    config=config,\n    version=\"v2\",\n)\n```\n\nAnd they require using the **same** `thread_id` in `config`.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## 9.5 Conditional interrupts\nConditional interrupts use a `when` predicate on `InterruptOnConfig`, receiving a `ToolCallRequest`. Docs note this requires `langchain>=1.3.3`.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\nExample from docs pattern:\n```python\nfrom langchain.agents.middleware import ToolCallRequest\n\ndef writes_outside_workspace(request: ToolCallRequest) -> bool:\n    path = request.tool_call[\"args\"].get(\"file_path\", \"\")\n    return not path.startswith(\"/workspace/\")\n```\n\n## 9.6 Filesystem permission interrupts\nThe docs also support approval via filesystem permission rules:\n```python\nFilesystemPermission(\n    operations=[\"write\"],\n    paths=[\"/secrets/**\"],\n    mode=\"interrupt\",\n)\n```\n\nThis requires **`deepagents>=0.6.8`**.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### Recommendation\nFor a research assistant:\n- put HITL on `write_file` and `edit_file` when writing to publishable/report destinations\n- optionally put HITL on external side-effect tools like `send_email` or `publish_report`\n- use permission-level `mode=\"interrupt\"` for protected paths like `/final/` or `/secrets/`\n\n---\n\n## 10) Proposed concrete implementation\n\n## 10.1 Main agent skeleton\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\nfrom deepagents.backends import CompositeBackend, StateBackend, FilesystemBackend\nfrom langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver\n\ndef internet_search(query: str, max_results: int = 5, topic: str = \"general\", include_raw_content: bool = False):\n    \"\"\"Run a web search.\"\"\"\n    ...\n\nbackend = CompositeBackend(\n    default=StateBackend(),\n    routes={\n        \"/workspace/\": FilesystemBackend(\n            root_dir=\"/absolute/path/to/research-project\",\n            virtual_mode=True,\n        ),\n    },\n)\n\nresearch_subagent = {\n    \"name\": \"researcher\",\n    \"description\": \"Conducts in-depth research and returns concise cited findings.\",\n    \"system_prompt\": (\n        \"You are a thorough researcher. Break the question into search queries, \"\n        \"gather evidence, and return a concise summary with source URLs.\"\n    ),\n    \"tools\": [internet_search],\n    \"model\": \"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n}\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"openai:gpt-5.5\",\n    tools=[internet_search],\n    system_prompt=(\n        \"You are a research assistant. \"\n        \"Use your todo list to plan work, delegate deep research to subagents, \"\n        \"store notes in /workspace/, and produce a final cited report.\"\n    ),\n    backend=backend,\n    subagents=[research_subagent],\n    interrupt_on={\n        \"write_file\": {\"allowed_decisions\": [\"approve\", \"edit\", \"reject\"]},\n        \"edit_file\": {\"allowed_decisions\": [\"approve\", \"edit\", \"reject\"]},\n    },\n    checkpointer=MemorySaver(),\n    name=\"research-assistant\",\n)\n```\n\nEvery API surface in this example comes from the documented/ referenced interfaces above.  \nSources:  \n- `create_deep_agent`: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent  \n- Backends: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- Subagents: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \n- HITL: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n## 10.2 Suggested agent workflow\n1. User asks a research question.\n2. Main agent writes a task list with `write_todos`.\n3. Main agent writes the request to `/workspace/request.md`.\n4. Main agent delegates subtopics to `researcher` via `task`.\n5. Subagent uses `internet_search`.\n6. Main agent consolidates findings into `/workspace/report_draft.md`.\n7. HITL gate reviews write/edit actions to final output.\n8. Main agent returns final answer with sources.\n\nThis pattern is well aligned with the Deep Agents overview and subagent docs.  \nSources:  \n- Overview: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview  \n- Subagents: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents\n\n---\n\n## 11) Engineering constraints and caveats\n\n### 11.1 Do not rely on default model selection\nThe reference says `model=None` is deprecated since `0.5.3`. Always pass `model=` explicitly.  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\n### 11.2 Use `CompositeBackend` instead of raw `FilesystemBackend`\nThe docs explicitly recommend this for keeping internal agent artifacts off real disk/project paths.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends\n\n### 11.3 HITL requires a checkpointer\nWithout `checkpointer=...`, pause/resume workflows are not supported.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop\n\n### 11.4 Permissions are only for built-in filesystem tools\nDocs state `permissions` do not cover arbitrary custom tools or MCP tools touching files.  \nSource: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/permissions\n\n### 11.5 `tools=` does not remove built-ins\nIf you need to hide built-ins, use harness profiles and `excluded_tools`.  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent\n\n### 11.6 Profiles API is beta\nThe `deepagents.profiles` API is labeled beta in the reference; use it carefully in production.  \nSource: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/profiles/harness/harness_profiles\n\n---\n\n## 12) Recommended first milestone\n\nImplement v1 with:\n- `deepagents==0.6.12`\n- explicit model string\n- one custom search tool\n- `CompositeBackend(default=StateBackend(), routes={\"/workspace/\": FilesystemBackend(...)})`\n- one declarative `researcher` subagent\n- `interrupt_on` for `write_file` and `edit_file`\n- `MemorySaver()` checkpointer for HITL\n\nThat gives the team:\n- planning\n- research delegation\n- workspace files\n- safe human approval\n- minimal complexity\n\n---\n\n## 13) Source index\n\n- PyPI package / version: https://pypi.org/project/deepagents/  \n- Deep Agents overview: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview  \n- Customize Deep Agents: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/customization  \n- Backends guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/backends  \n- Permissions guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/permissions  \n- Subagents guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents  \n- Human-in-the-loop guide: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/human-in-the-loop  \n- Going to production: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/going-to-production  \n- API reference root: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/  \n- `create_deep_agent` reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/graph/create_deep_agent  \n- Agent reference page: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/agent  \n- Harness profiles reference: https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/profiles/harness/harness_profiles  \n\nShort answer: use **`deepagents==0.6.12`**, build around **`create_deep_agent(...)`** with a **`CompositeBackend`**, define research workers in **`subagents=`**, and enable approval with **`interrupt_on` + `checkpointer`**.",
